items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: It might be simply that I was so affected by Teschmacher's and Jacobson's and Bud Freeman's playing, when I was awakening to music

ctx.x: Bud Jacobson developed his ear, so that that, to the point that that intonation was correct. And this, I think, he leaned on, uh, Teschmacher's lead, and said, uh, we can get an effect by playing flat, or, it doesn't matter if you play flat, but it was on the flat side. It wasn't on the sharp side. The bud would usually err.

I think that's true, and that's a problem that's been bothering me ever since I started to play. I'm afraid that, uh, myself, I have, uh, difficulties. I, I tend to play flat. Now, I don't know, uh, as you suggest, the, the, uh, causes, probable causes for this. It might be deficiency in ear. It might be simply that I was so affected by Teschmacher's and Jacobson's and Bud Freeman's playing, when I was awakening to music, that I, uh, adapted this flat feeling about, about playing. You know, Bud played quite flat…
No, you know, uh, well, one other name before we go, uh, connect this back to New Orleans. Burkhoff.
